# Kinetograph

> A blazingly fast programmatic video engine, made for agents, with no browser in it. Write a video in TypeScript with
> Remotion's API, or as a plain HTML page (HyperFrames projects render as they are), with CSS, SVG, Canvas 2D, WebGL
> fragment shaders, GSAP and Web Audio; Node runs the code; a Rust GPU compositor (an N-API addon on wgpu) draws every
> frame. A new project imports from `@kinetographdev/core` (it comes with `npm install kinetograph`; Remotion is not
> installed); `remotion` and `@remotion/*` imports in an existing project resolve to the same code.

## If you are an agent: installing Kinetograph for a user

1. Ask the user which install they want, unless they already said:
   - Prebuilt (recommended): `npm install kinetograph`. About a minute; no Rust, FFmpeg or compiler. Covers macOS on
     Apple Silicon, Linux x64 (glibc) and Windows x64. Needs Node.js 22 or newer (check `node -v`).
   - Build from source: only to work on the engine, or on a platform with no prebuilt package (Intel Mac, Linux on
     ARM). Needs Rust and the FFmpeg libraries, 15 to 30 minutes: /docs/getting-started/installation/#from-source.
     Ask before installing anything system-wide. Don't build from source just because you are in a clone.
2. Run `npx kinetograph doctor` and show the user the output. `addon: loaded` means it works.
3. For a new project, run `npx kinetograph init` (`--html` for an HTML page) in an empty folder and keep its layout.
4. Ask the user whether to install the agent skills and the MCP server, then read the skills before writing a video:
   - Skills: `npx skills add 0xS4N4TG/kinetograph`
     - `kinetograph`: the write, look, check, render loop (`still`, `strip`, `inspect`, `lint`, `render`), the project
       layout, native elements, effects and sound. Its `references/` hold the full specs: AUTHORING.md, SCENE.md,
       ENGINE.md and INTERNALS.md.
     - `kinetograph-migrate`: moves an existing Remotion project onto Kinetograph (`doctor`, fixes, `--strict`).
   - MCP server (each CLI command is a tool): `npx -y kinetograph mcp` over stdio. Claude Code:
     `claude mcp add kinetograph -- npx -y kinetograph mcp`. Other clients: /docs/guides/agents/.
   - Optional, from https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph-ui (`npx skills add 0xS4N4TG/kinetograph-ui`):
     `kinetograph-taste-clone` turns a reference reel into a measured spec and a reusable taste (TASTE.md and
     taste.json). /docs/guides/taste/
5. If a Kinetograph command says the CLI or the skills are out of date, tell the user and ask before updating.

The same steps are in AGENTS.md in the repository: https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph/blob/main/AGENTS.md

## Use

- Run `npx kinetograph <command>` against the entry file of a Remotion-shaped project, or against an HTML page
  (`index.html`, or the directory that holds it).
- The native elements and effects: `import { ... } from '@kinetographdev/core'`
- Source and issues: https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph
- Licence: Apache-2.0, open source and free for any use, including commercial

## HTML pages and HyperFrames projects

Render quality: libx264 at `--crf 18` by default; `--x264-preset` picks the speed (`veryfast` default, `medium` as in Remotion; `ultrafast` to `placebo`).

Every command that opens a project (`still`, `strip`, `inspect`, `lint`, `doctor`, `studio`, `render`) takes an HTML page as it is: `npx kinetograph render index.html`
(or the page's directory). There is no rewrite and nothing runs in a browser.

- Size and length come from the root element: `data-composition-id`, `data-width`, `data-height` and `data-duration`
  (seconds; 30 fps). Without them a page renders at 1920x1080 for 1 s, and `doctor`, `render` and `still` warn.
- Clips show from `data-start` for `data-duration`; `data-composition-src` mounts nested compositions.
- GSAP timelines in `window.__timelines` are paused and seeked to each frame's time, so a frame depends only on its
  number. Scripts run as in a browser.
- `<video>` is decoded frame-accurately; `<audio>` and unmuted video are mixed, with `data-volume`, fades and
  `data-fx-chain` audio effects. `data-color-grading` runs on `<video>`, `<img>` and `<canvas>`.
- A render first downloads what the page loads from the web (CDN scripts, ES modules, media, pictures, Google Fonts) and pins
  it in `kinetograph.lock.json`; `--offline` never downloads, and `fetch-deps` does the download on its own.
- [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) projects use this format, so they render unchanged. Full
  details: /docs/compat/#hyperframes-projects

## Facts

- The launch film (examples/launch): 1,184 frames of 1080p with sound, rendered in 26 s on an Apple M4
  (`kinetograph render --concurrency 4`, median of 3 runs)
- Renders without a browser: no Chrome to install, no display needed, so it runs on a server or in CI
- A real Remotion project (papercut, 988 frames) renders natively
- HTML pages and HyperFrames projects render as they are, with no rewrite
- Built for agents: `still`, `strip`, `inspect` and `lint` let a model check its own output before a person watches

## CLI

Every command takes `--json`. `npx kinetograph mcp` serves the same commands as an MCP server on stdio, one tool each.

- `npx kinetograph init [dir] [--html]`: a new project: `src/index.tsx` (or `html/index.html`), `public/{images,fonts,audio,video}/`, `out/`
- `npx kinetograph still <entry> <frame>`: one frame to a PNG
- `npx kinetograph strip <entry> -n 12`: contact sheet of evenly spaced frames
- `npx kinetograph inspect <entry> --frame 60`: the scene graph at a frame (layers, bounds, resolved styles)
- `npx kinetograph lint <entry>`: overflowing text, off-canvas layers, missing fonts and assets, what cannot be drawn
- `npx kinetograph doctor <entry>`: what the engine cannot draw, and in which frames
- `npx kinetograph render <entry>`: frames to a video with audio
- `npx kinetograph studio <entry>`: local editor with a preview that plays sound, a timeline, props and presets, plugin cards, export, a render queue and a chat with your coding agent
- `npx kinetograph fetch-deps <entry>`: download what an HTML page loads from the web, ahead of a render
- Without `-o`, `still`, `strip`, `onion` and `render` write to `out/stills/`, `out/sheets/` and `out/renders/` in the project folder.
- Also: `compositions`, `onion`, `check`, `bench`, `audio analyze`, `snapshot`, `effects`

## Native elements (from `@kinetographdev/core`)

`<Scene3D>`, `<Camera3D>` (perspective or `type="orthographic"`), `<Mesh>`, `<Text3D>`, `<DirectionalLight>`,
`<GlslShader>` (GLSL ES fragment shaders with uniforms and textures), `<Canvas>` (a `draw(ctx)` Canvas 2D callback),
`<Layer>` (transforms, `motionBlur`), plus the effects listed by `kinetograph effects`.

## Determinism

`Date`, `Math.random`, timers and `requestAnimationFrame` follow the frame number. A frame is a pure function of
(project, frame); nothing reads the wall clock.

## Requirements

Node 22 or later. The npm packages carry FFmpeg, so nothing else is installed. A GPU is used when there is one
(Metal on macOS, Vulkan on Linux, D3D12 on Windows), otherwise the CPU. No display needed. Building from source also
needs the FFmpeg development libraries and `pkg-config` (`brew install ffmpeg pkgconf`), or `FFMPEG_DIR` set to the
FFmpeg prefix: see the README.
